title: Select an area and mask it
summary: Draw a selection, turn it into a layer mask and switch it off and on.

steps.say: In the Layers tab, click the photo layer so it is highlighted.

check.prompt: Is the photo layer highlighted in the Layers tab?

hints: It is usually the bottom row.
Press Control L if the Layers tab is not showing.
steps.why: Selections and masks act on the highlighted layer.

steps.say: Press F for Free Select, then click around your subject, ending on the first point.

check.prompt: Is there a dashed selection outline around an object in the photo?

hints: Press Enter to close and confirm the shape if clicking the first point is tricky.
For a plain background, press U for Fuzzy Select and click the background, then press Control I.
steps.why: The selection tells GIMP which part of the photo to keep.

steps.say: Open the Layer menu, then Mask, then Add Layer Mask.

checks.prompt: Is a dialog open listing ways to start the layer mask, such as White and Selection?

hints: The Layer menu is in the menu bar at the top.
Right-clicking the layer in the Layers tab shows Add Layer Mask too.
steps.why: A mask hides parts of a layer without deleting pixels.

steps.say: Choose Selection in the list, then click Add.

check.prompt: Does the layer now show a mask thumbnail, with everything outside the selection hidden or transparent?

hints: Selection is one of the options under Initialize Layer Mask to.
If the result is reversed, undo and tick Invert Mask before clicking Add.
steps.why: Starting from the selection gives the mask the right shape at once.

steps.say: Press Control Shift A to remove the selection outline.

checks.prompt: Is the dashed selection outline gone from the image?

hints: Select, then None in the menu bar does the same.
The mask stays; only the outline goes away.
steps.why: Leftover selections limit later edits in confusing ways.

steps.say: Open Layer, then Mask, and tick Disable Layer Mask to see the full photo.

check.prompt: Is the full photo visible again, with the mask thumbnail outlined in red?

hints: Open the same menu and untick it to turn the mask back on.
Right-clicking the layer shows the same option.
steps.why: Switching a mask off proves that nothing was deleted.
